title: Simulation: add a step button that jumps to the start of the next operation

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> when hitting simulation there sh ould be an option to "step" thru to next operation.. so we can check the one relevant

## Problem

The simulation plays the whole program from the first move. A user who wants to check one operation must scrub or wait. There is no way to go to the next operation.

## Wanted

1. The simulation controls have a "next operation" step. It moves the playback position to the first move of the next operation in program order.
2. A matching "previous operation" step. It moves to the start of the current operation, and a second press moves to the start of the one before it.
3. The control shows which operation is current (its name from the tree). A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change works the same as a step inside one setup.
4. The stock shown at the new position is correct: it is the stock after all earlier operations. A step must give the same stock as playback to that position. A step never skips a removal.
5. Disabled states: "next" is disabled in the last operation. "previous" is disabled at the start of the first operation. The AccessKit labels and the tooltips say what each button does.
6. A keyboard shortcut for each step, listed in the shortcut help.

## Notes

- The playback position is ephemeral UI state (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"), so no undoable command is needed. If a step selects an operation in the tree, that selection goes through `SelectEntity`.
- A skipped or suppressed operation is not a stop. An operation with no toolpath is not a stop.
- UI text: plain English, no G-code jargon. A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and the position, not pixel values (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`).
- Related: #2587 (the stand-alone simulator window). The same step logic should work there. Keep the operation-boundary lookup in the lowest crate that provides it, so both can use it.

## Done means

- A test shows that "next" from a position inside operation 1 gives the first move of operation 2, and that the stock equals the stock from plain playback to that move.
- Tests for the first operation, the last operation, a tool change and an operation with no toolpath.
- The behaviour tests and the page layout test of the simulation panel pass.
